summary.tldr: Creates a new offence for breaching release conditions in some serious cases and bars more offenders from serving sentences in the community.
what_it_does: Creates a new offence for people on conditional release for offences in Schedules I or II of the Corrections and Conditional Release Act who, without reasonable excuse, break a condition of parole, statutory release or temporary absence.
Allows that breach to be prosecuted as an indictable offence with up to 2 years in prison, or as a summary conviction offence.
Expands the offences that cannot get a conditional sentence, including some indictable offences with maximum penalties of 14 years or life.

Also bars conditional sentences for some 10-year indictable offences involving bodily harm, drugs or weapons, and for listed offences such as sexual assault, kidnapping and arson for fraudulent purpose.

Requires parole supervisors to report certain breaches by offenders on conditional release or long-term supervision to the Parole Board of Canada, the Service, the Attorney General and the local police force.
summary.background: The bill changes the Criminal Code rules on conditional sentences and the Corrections and Conditional Release Act rules on parole, statutory release and long-term supervision.
